Definition: from G575 and G1183; to tithe (as debtor or creditor):--(give, pay, take) tithe.
BiblicalUsage: To tithe — to give or take the tenth. The sons of Levi have a commandment to take tithes of the people according to the law in Hebrews 7:5, and the Pharisee in Luke 18:12 boasts that he gives tithes of all he possesses. But Jesus turns the word into a rebuke in Luke 11:42 and Matthew 23:23: they tithe mint and rue and cummin, and pass over judgment and the love of God, omitting the weightier matters of the law.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the tithe was never the problem; the problem was tithing the garden herbs while starving justice and mercy. The tenth belongs to God, and Jesus says so plainly — these ought ye to have done — but a tithe that costs me nothing of my heart is no tithe at all. I hold that giving is measured by what I pass over, not by what I count.
